content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to change the communication port number? I'm currently using [article_no].
Welcome to the forum. I believe you do not have a [product_name] [article_no]. Most likely, it's another version or order number, possibly ending with [article_no].

Hi, thank you for the warm welcome and the quick reply. My device is this: [company_name] [product_name] [article_no]. Is it possible to connect with this PLC using Visual Studio? I've tried the sample code, but couldn't get it to work. The code attempts to connect via port 10001 instead of 8080, so the PLC doesn't connect. Any solutions to this? Thank you very much.

I've attached an excerpt from the manual showing all the ports used by the current [product_name] for exchanging data with devices or software. Typically, port 102 is commonly used and works for many scenarios. I am not familiar with Visual Studio, so I can't provide assistance with its configuration.

Directly changing the port is not possible. [product_name] also does not support DHCP. However, you can connect it to an extra router's LAN port and link the router's WAN port to your main network. This allows you to use the additional router's DHCP to assign an IP address, and utilize port forwarding to direct chosen ports to the [product_name]'s port. For example, if [product_name] uses IP 192.168.1.10 and port 8080, while your network operates on 192.168.2.x and you want communication on port 10001, you can set up the extra router accordingly and configure port forwarding from 10001 to 8080. If you prefer a static IP, you can manually configure the additional router's WAN interface to use a static address within your main network's subnet.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members find it challenging to set up communication links between [product_name] PLCs and their applications, mainly because the communication port is fixed on the PLC and cannot be custom configured. This limitation creates incompatibility with third-party tools or example codes that expect different port assignments, preventing easy integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to customize or configure the communication port on their [product_name] PLCs to suit their application needs and facilitate direct integration with Visual Studio or similar development environments.
